Goal: Run the FULL verification (ruff + complete pytest incl. torch-gated test_packs.py) for the merged main branch, in its worktree. Report only — no repo edits needed; if you must fix trivial breakage, keep it minimal and uncommitted.

Workspace: worktree /Users/sachinkoli/.hoocode/worktrees/clone-your-voice/fulltest, branch agent/fulltest, base 3426b83 (parent repo /Users/sachinkoli/github/clone-your-voice). Work read-only except a worktree-local .venv (gitignored) and /tmp scratch. Use `git -C <worktree>`; never commit or push.

Context: main just merged three branches: M3 `cyv watermark detect` (new daemon op/CLI/tests), hygiene (portable pid_alive, 2 new socket tests, licenses, B0 doc, CI activation), M1 benchmark docs. Prior runs were partial: M3 worktree 158 passed/6 skipped with test_packs.py uncollectable (no torch); hygiene tests validated only via ad-hoc python (no pytest installed). Nothing has run the full suite with torch yet.

Constraints: NO brew (user forbids it). Build the env with direct downloads only: system python3 -m venv (or uv via https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh + `uv python install 3.12` if 3.12 is needed — kokoro/misaki need <3.13, but for TESTS you only need dev extras + torch CPU; try system python first, fall back to uv-python 3.12). CAUTION: tests/test_packs.py does a top-level `import torch` — that plus sanitize tests may download weights; do NOT download model weights — if a test needs weights/network, let it fail/skip and report it as blocked-with-reason rather than fetching. Steps:
1. Create .venv in worktree, install dev extras + torch (CPU/arm64 wheel).
2. `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .`.
3. `python -m pytest` full (default, no CYV_E2E).
4. If failures: diagnose whether caused by the merged branches (M3/hygiene) vs pre-existing env issues; fix ONLY trivial merge breakage, else report.

Done when: full suite result (pass/fail counts, failures listed) + ruff result are reported, or blocked-with-reason for any unrunnable part.

Report: status complete/partial/failed; ruff + pytest results with counts; per-failure diagnosis (merged-code bug vs env vs weights); files changed if any (must stay uncommitted); scratch paths.
